properties.name: MEASURED — one process, four designs: the intercept is 17 MB and the slope ~5 MB and 7 fds per open design. flo2's item 2, takeable for the first time
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-09-13 on the release binary, one process serving four designs under one registry root over `/g/<graph_id>/`, each attached in turn. THIS MEASUREMENT COULD NOT BE TAKEN BEFORE TODAY: it needs one process holding several designs, and nothing called `Registry::discover` outside its own tests.

    designs open   RSS      fds     delta
    0              17 MB     10             <- INTERCEPT, per process
    1 (+alpha)     32 MB     17     +15 MB  +7 fds
    2 (+beta)      39 MB     24     + 7 MB  +7 fds
    3 (+gamma)     44 MB     31     + 5 MB  +7 fds
    4 (+delta)     49 MB     38     + 5 MB  +7 fds

    intercept ~17 MB / 10 fds per PROCESS
    slope     ~5 MB / 7 fds per OPEN DESIGN at steady state

⭐ WHAT THIS DECIDES, which is the question flo2 asked it for: one service holding many graphs against a process per project. Process-per-project pays the 17 MB intercept EVERY time; one service pays it once and ~5 MB per design after. At four designs that is 49 MB against roughly 68 MB, and the gap widens linearly. The fd slope is exact and constant at 7 per design, which is the number that matters for a cap — dec:one-process-many-stores warns that N designs is N sets of file handles, and now it is 7N plus 10.

⚠️ THE FIRST OPEN COSTS 15 MB AND THE REST COST 5. That one-time warm-up is not per-design cost and must not be multiplied: quoting 15 MB per design would overstate a fifty-design server by 500 MB.

🛑 THESE ARE NEAR-EMPTY DESIGNS, SO THE SLOPE IS A FLOOR AND NOT AN ESTIMATE. Each store was freshly minted with almost no nodes. A real design adds its own data on top: measured the same day, reflow2's own 4,403-node design opened in a dedicated process sits at 62 MB against a 19 MB store-less floor — about 43 MB for that one store. Per-design cost therefore scales with design size, and 5 MB is what an EMPTY design costs to hold, not what a working one does.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: the slope for designs of realistic size in one process (only the floor was measured); whether it stays linear past four; and the behaviour at the `--registry-max-open` cap, which refuses rather than evicts. No idle eviction exists, so a long-lived server's high-water mark is the number of DISTINCT designs ever asked for, not the number in use.
